qualitative_findings.claim: Sign of P_Z follows the enantiomer: (M) negative, (P) positive, on all three substrates.
On Cu(332) P_Z is independent of the light polarization.
On Ag and Au the intrinsic substrate polarization from circular light adds to the CISS contribution (~±8%).
ΔP_Z is similar on substrates with very different SOC (11.7, 15.9, 15.7%), so substrate SOC is not the dominant factor.
Model: |P_Z| increases with the number of helical turns; sign flips with helicity and varies with energy.

discrepancies.description: SI says (P)-[7]H shifts cw polarization on Au from -24.2% to -16.0%, 'i.e., by +7.8%'; arithmetic gives +8.2%. (ccw: +7.4%; their mean is 7.8%.)
Table 1 gives no uncertainties; text gives ±0.6% (Cu) and ±0.4-0.5% for (P)/Au only.
Annealing '400 °C and 600 °C, for Ag and Cu and Au, respectively' - three metals, two temperatures; mapping ambiguous.
120 / 76 recorded spin polarizations for (M)/(P) on Cu(332) are totals; per-polarization counts only in Fig. 2.
Fig. S2 x-axis labels lack minus signs (50 ... 0 ... 50); negative side inferred from text values.
